title: Grove caps how fast capital can enter an allocation but leaves withdrawal limits unlimited or unset
content:
The asymmetry recurs across unrelated venues. A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.9.2.2.4.2 gives a withdrawal `maxAmount` of "N/A" against a 50,000,000 USDC deposit limit; A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.12.2.2.4.2 gives "Unlimited" withdrawals against a 25,000,000 deposit cap; A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.12.3.2.4.2 gives "Unlimited" on the aggregate *and* both per-asset withdrawal limits.

The implied doctrine is that rate limits exist to bound the *rate of risk accumulation*, not to control Grove's balance sheet generally. A deposit limit answers "how fast can we become exposed to a counterparty we may have mis-assessed?" — a question about the speed of an irreversible mistake. A withdrawal limit would answer "how fast can we stop being exposed?", and throttling that is straightforwardly harmful.

This is the opposite of the convention in the protocols Grove allocates *into*, where withdrawal throttling protects a pool from a run. Grove is the depositor, not the pool, so the risk it is managing points the other way.

The non-obvious consequence: rate limits provide no protection against Grove exiting a position badly — dumping size, realizing losses, or draining a venue Sky depends on. Whatever governs exit quality lives elsewhere (slippage bounds, operational processes), not in the rate-limit layer. Where an Instance *does* bound withdrawals, as at A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.10.1.2.4.2, that is a deliberate departure worth reading as a venue-specific concern rather than the norm.
description: Withdrawal maxAmount reads N/A or Unlimited across most Instances while deposits are strictly bounded, making rate limiting a risk-accumulation brake rather than an exit control.
